title: The exact sequence of supported sections for injective objects
statement:
For the closed–open pair of
supported sections and a termwise
injective complex $I^\bullet$ of $\Lambda$-module sheaves, there is
a short exact sequence of complexes

$$
0\longrightarrow s_*s^!I^\bullet\longrightarrow I^\bullet
\longrightarrow j_*j^*I^\bullet\longrightarrow0.
$$

proof.text: Work on compatible representatives of $\mathcal C=X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ in the size convention of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], with $\mathcal O=\Lambda_X$. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], $U_{\mathrm{proet}}=\mathcal C/U$, $\Lambda_U=\mathcal O|_U$, and $U\to X$ is a monomorphism. The restriction of a sheaf $M$ to $U$ has value $M(W)$ on $(W\to U)$, as in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. This is the inverse image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]: for $W\to U$, the category $\mathcal I_W$ there has initial object $(W,W\to U\times_XW)$, with the diagonal arrow. A morphism from this object to $(V,\phi)$ must be the second component $W\to V$ of $\phi$, and this component does define that unique morphism. Thus the opposite indexing category has a final object, its colimit is $M(W)$, and sheafification changes nothing because restriction is a sheaf. Apply this calculation also to rings and module actions. Under $j^{-1}\Lambda_X=\Lambda_X|_U$, the coefficient map $c^j_\Lambda:j^{-1}\Lambda_X\to\Lambda_U$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] sends each constant section $\lambda$ to $\lambda$: its adjoint $\rho^j_\Lambda$ was defined that way, and the initial-object calculation evaluates the adjunction on that same section. Consequently $c^j_\Lambda$ is the inverse of the isomorphism $\Lambda_U\to\Lambda_X|_U$ in clause (2) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], since the composite is the unique sheaf-of-rings map extending the identity on constants. The module pullback $j^*M=j^{-1}M\otimes_{j^{-1}\Lambda_X}\Lambda_U$ is therefore restriction as an $\Lambda_U$-module: after this coefficient identification, the sectionwise maps $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$ and $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ are inverse and commute with restrictions, so remain inverse after sheafification. The module unit is the abelian-sheaf unit followed by $x\mapsto x\otimes1$; under these identifications it is still restriction. For $V\to X$ in $\mathcal C$, put $V_U=V\times_XU$. The same two cited statements ensure $V_U$ is an object of $\mathcal C$. The direct-image formula now gives $(j_*j^*M)(V)=M(V_U)$, and the unit at $V$ is the restriction $M(V)\to M(V_U)$.

source.place: Proof, the restriction map on V and V times_X U; expanded using the localization and inverse-image definitions

proof.text: For any object $T$ of $\mathcal C$, let $P_T=\mathcal O[h_T]$ be the free module presheaf of [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module], and let $L_T=P_T^\#$ be its module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For $a:V_U\to V$, the induced map $P_{V_U}\to P_V$ sends $e_b$ to $e_{ab}$ on each object $T$. This is a presheaf morphism: for $c:T'\to T$, either order of applying restriction and this map sends $r e_b$ to $r|_c e_{abc}$; hence the component maps commute with all restrictions. The map $\operatorname{Hom}(T,V_U)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,V)$ is injective: two arrows with equal $V$-components also have equal $U$-components because $U\to X$ is a monomorphism, and then agree by the pullback universal property. Consequently each component on free modules is injective: a left inverse on that component retains coefficients on basis elements in this image and discards all others. This componentwise injectivity implies that the presheaf morphism is a monomorphism, since equality after it can be cancelled at every object. By exactness of module sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact], its sheafification $L_{V_U}\to L_V$ is a monomorphism. No naturality of the componentwise left inverses is asserted or needed.

source.place: Remark Tag 03EJ (remark-localize-presheaves); Lemma Tag 03EI (lemma-sheafification-exact); free-basis injection written out

proof.text: The module sheafification adjunction of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] and the explicit bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] identify $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(L_T,M)$ with $M(T)$: a section $x\in M(T)$ corresponds before sheafification to $e_b\mapsto x|_b$. Precomposition by $L_{V_U}\to L_V$ therefore corresponds exactly to restriction along $a:V_U\to V$: on the identity generator of $V_U$ the composite takes the value $x|_a$. This establishes the required compatibility in the represented object, rather than assuming it from naturality in the coefficient sheaf.

source.place: Remark Tag 03EJ (remark-localize-presheaves); equation-map-lower-shriek-OU-into-module after Lemma Tag 03DI; direct generator calculation

proof.text: Fix a degree $r$ and an arbitrary $V$ in $\mathcal C$. For $y\in I^r(V_U)$, step 3 gives a morphism $L_{V_U}\to I^r$. Extend it across the monomorphism $L_{V_U}\to L_V$ of step 2, using injectivity of $I^r$ in the precise sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The resulting morphism corresponds to $x\in I^r(V)$ with $x|_{V_U}=y$ by step 3. Hence the unit $\eta^r:I^r\to j_*j^*I^r$ is surjective on sections over every $V$, by step 1. It is an epimorphism of sheaves: if two morphisms from $j_*j^*I^r$ have equal composites with $\eta^r$, evaluate at any $V$ and lift any section by this surjectivity to see that their components agree on every section. The morphisms are therefore equal.

source.place: Proof, applying Hom(-,I) to the free-module monomorphism and proving the last surjectivity term by term

proof.text:
By [def-pur-flasque-support], in each degree
$\mathcal G_ZI^r=\ker(\eta^r)=s_*s^!I^r$, with the displayed equality supplying the canonical kernel identification; kernels of module sheaves are computed sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Naturality of restriction gives $\eta^{r+1}d_I^r=(j_*j^*d_I^r)\eta^r$. Thus $d_I^r$ restricts to $\delta^r:\mathcal G_ZI^r\to\mathcal G_ZI^{r+1}$, equivalently to the differential on $s_*s^!I^\bullet$, and $\delta^{r+1}\delta^r=0$ by cancellation of the kernel inclusion. The kernel inclusions and the units form morphisms of complexes, with zero composite. In each degree the inclusion is monic, its image is the kernel of $\eta^r$, and $\eta^r$ is epic by step 4. Therefore the sequence is short exact in each degree by [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence].

source.place: Proof, first sentence identifying the kernel, and its termwise extension to the given complex

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cochain-complexes-degreewise-exact] to the abelian category of $\Lambda_X$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Step 5 supplies the complex maps and their zero composite, and steps 4--5 supply short exactness in every integer degree. Its degreewise criterion gives the asserted short exact sequence of complexes $0\to s_*s^!I^\bullet\to I^\bullet\to j_*j^*I^\bullet\to0$. No boundedness of the complex and no K-injectivity are used.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0114 (lemma-cat-cochain-abelian), degreewise short exactness criterion
